summary.text: Climate change today means global warming, the ongoing rise in Earth's average temperature, together with its wider effects on the climate system.
Burning coal, oil and gas releases greenhouse gases that absorb some of the heat Earth gives off after sunlight warms it, warming the lower atmosphere.
It brings more heat waves, wildfires, intense storms and droughts, and some effects such as sea level rise will continue for centuries.

facts.label: Extra carbon dioxide
facts.value: Roughly 50% more than at the pre-industrial era's end

items.prompt: A city's power comes mostly from coal. How does burning that coal end up warming the lower atmosphere?

options.label: The smoke blocks sunlight from reaching the ground
The heat from the furnaces spreads into the sky
It releases gases that absorb heat the Earth gives off
It thins the ozone layer, letting more sunlight in

items.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases, which absorb some of the heat Earth radiates after sunlight warms it.

items.prompt: A country cuts its emissions to zero tomorrow. What happens to sea level rise and ocean warming?

options.label: They stop within a few years
They reverse within a decade
They speed up sharply at first
They keep going for centuries

items.explain: Even if efforts to limit future warming succeed, ocean heating, ocean acidification and sea level rise will continue for centuries.

items.prompt: About 20,000 years ago, at the last ice age peak, Earth was some 5–7 °C colder than now. Roughly how far below today's level was the sea?

options.label: About 2 metres
About 15 metres
Over 125 metres
Over 1,000 metres

items.explain: During the most recent glacial maximum, sea levels were over 125 metres lower than today.

items.prompt: A small farming nation has produced very little of the world's emissions. How does climate change tend to affect such poorer communities?

options.label: They are most vulnerable and least able to adapt
They are spared because they emit so little
They gain most from longer growing seasons
They face risk only once warming passes 2 °C

items.explain: Poorer communities cause a small share of emissions yet have the least ability to adapt and are the most vulnerable.

items.prompt: A friend says 'global warming' and 'climate change' mean exactly the same thing. How do scientists tell them apart?

options.label: Global warming covers rain; climate change covers heat
Climate change adds warming's effects, like rain shifts
Global warming is natural; climate change is human
Climate change refers only to the oceans' warming

items.explain: Global warming is just the rise in average surface temperature; climate change includes that warming plus its effects, such as changes in precipitation.

items.prompt: Before the 1980s, scientists were unsure whether human pollution would warm or cool the planet overall. What was the cooling side of that question?

options.label: Ice sheets reflecting more sunlight each year
A dimming Sun during the solar cycle
Forests absorbing all the extra carbon dioxide
Airborne particles from air pollution

items.explain: It was unclear whether greenhouse gas warming outweighed the cooling effect of airborne particulates in polluted air.
